name: Surveyor 3
tagline: I proved you could land on the Moon… and two astronauts came to visit me.
discovery: With my little scoop, I dug into the lunar soil and showed it was firm enough to hold a crewed spacecraft. My pictures helped prepare the Apollo missions.
status_note: Silent since May 1967. My camera is missing: astronauts took it back to Earth!

presentation.title: They say old friends always come back. I'm Surveyor 3.
presentation.body: I'm a lander from the Surveyor 3 mission. I proved you could land on the Moon… and two astronauts came to visit me.

chapters.title: A bouncing landing
chapters.body: On 20 April 1967, I descend toward the Ocean of Storms. My engines were supposed to shut off just before touchdown… but they stay on! I bounce twice before coming to a stop. Phew, I'm in one piece.

chapters.title: My scoop and my pictures
chapters.body: I have a camera and a small arm with a scoop. For two weeks, I dig trenches and send back thousands of pictures. On Earth, engineers learn how the soil reacts when you press on it: exactly what they need to know to land a module with astronauts.

chapters.title: The Apollo 12 visit
chapters.body: When the long lunar night falls, I go to sleep forever. But in November 1969, Apollo 12 lands about 180 metres from me! Astronauts Pete Conrad and Alan Bean walk over, cut off my camera and a few parts, and bring them back to Earth. Scientists could then study what 31 months on the Moon had done to my materials.

quiz.question: Why did Surveyor 3 bounce when it landed?
choices: Its engines did not shut off in time
quiz.explanation: Its small braking engines stayed on all the way to the ground. It bounced twice before settling for good.

quiz.question: Which crewed mission came to visit Surveyor 3?
quiz.explanation: In 1969, the Apollo 12 crew landed nearby and brought its camera back to Earth.
